explanation:
断, formerly 斷, combines 斤, an axe, with the thread design 㡭. The threads are stretched on a loom and severed across the middle. The axe identifies the act that cuts them apart.

From cutting the threads, 断 means to sever, break off, or interrupt something generally. A connection can be ended; an activity can be stopped; a demand can be refused.

Cutting also supplies the force of a decision. An unsettled matter is brought to an end by determining what will be done. Thus 断 extends to deciding, judging, and making a firm resolution, as well as the physical breaking of continuity shown in the older graph.
